purpose: Repair D1 in chunk BODIES and HEADINGS: HTML comments and other markup were never stripped from indexed evidence, so pipeline metadata reached the answer model. NOTE: the chunk TITLE is derived on a separate path this package does not touch and is NOT covered - see escalation.
codex_rationale: D1 is the prompt-contamination path: it decides what text from an untrusted note reaches the answer model. It also changes chunking and therefore index content. Three previous attempts were destructive and one reached Codex, which found what Agent C had passed. The high-risk criteria are met.

previous_attempts.failure: the fence pattern r"(?m)^\\s*```[^`]*$" had both \s and [^`] crossing line boundaries, so it ran from a fence line to a later line end and deleted the fenced code and all prose after the closing fence. The base was inert, so the repair was strictly worse than the defect. Found by Agent C.

scoping the patterns to one line fixed that, but cleanup still ran OVER fenced content, deleting an HTML comment's inner lines and a rule inside a fenced example. Found by Codex after Agent C had passed it.

fence-awareness was added inside flush(), which sees only one chunk, so a chunk boundary falling inside a fence stranded the rest of it. Found by Agent C; the package was withdrawn with the budget exhausted.

history.why_this_one_is_different: the previous three edited the pattern; this one moves markup handling out of flush() into a whole-note, line-local classifier that runs before chunking, so no pattern can span lines and the boundary decisions can see markup.

design.new_function: classify_markup(lines, fm_end) -> one dict per line with number, kind (keep/drop), text, fenced
properties: every decision is line-local, so a marker pattern cannot span lines whatever it is written as
inside a fenced block nothing is stripped; the content is carried verbatim
HTML comments outside a fence are removed with per-line state, so a comment spanning lines is handled a line at a time and two comments on one line cannot merge
the main loop iterates classified lines, so a '#' line inside a fence is not a heading and cannot split the chunk
the span is protected by the 'if line.strip()' guard in the main loop, not by dropped lines being skipped. Agent C demonstrated the latter is not load-bearing; the earlier wording claimed it was.
design.flush_now_contains: the two whitespace collapses, with their doubled backslashes corrected, and the readable-signal gate

defects_repaired.effect: In chunk BODIES and HEADINGS, outside a fenced block: HTML comments - inline, several per line, spanning lines, closing mid-line, and sharing a line with an unterminated opener - are removed with all surrounding prose kept, as are standalone rules and fence delimiters. Inside a fenced block nothing is removed. A comment containing a fence delimiter is removed in full. An unterminated comment removes nothing and is kept as literal text. This does NOT extend to the chunk TITLE, which note_title derives from the raw lines before classify_markup runs.
defects_repaired.scope_limit_found_by_agent_c: Three revisions of this field were stated unqualified and were therefore false. Agent C caught the overstatement in each. The qualification above is the correction.

defects_still_open_and_still_pinned.why_not_here: needs the reranker to take matched terms from what FTS5 returned instead of re-deriving them by string comparison
coupled to D5: deterministic_evidence_strength returns HIGH for any all_terms match however few or generic the terms are, so every change to the term set moves strength as a side effect

index_effect.measured: base and candidate built over the same fixture vault, re-measured for this candidate
index_effect.10 Areas/Fenced Markup Note.md: 2 chunks on base -> 1 on candidate: the heading-like line inside the fence no longer splits it
index_effect.correction: the previous revision of this block carried candidate 44e75883's numbers (12 notes, 10 of 12) and was stale. Agent C caught it.

known_limitations: T1, the residual Agent C blocked on: the chunk TITLE is derived by note_title from the RAW lines, before classify_markup runs, so a '# ' line inside a complete HTML comment or inside a fence becomes the note's title. That title is indexed in chunks_fts at bm25 weight 5.00 (the highest column weight), contributes to the coverage reranker's haystack, and is printed as 'Title: ...' in the evidence block handed to the answer model. For a note with no other indexable content the fallback also carries it into the chunk body. Pre-existing and identical on the base; not touched by this package.

REINDEX REQUIRED: chunk bodies and, for a note with a heading-like line inside a fence, chunk BOUNDARIES both change. An index built before this commit carries marker text in its bodies. Nothing here rebuilds an existing database.

Tilde (~~~) fences and lines of four or more backticks are still not recognised as fences, so their contents are NOT protected from stripping. Pre-existing scope; now materially relevant because the stripping is live for the first time.

Fence markers are removed from the evidence a note contributes, so a fenced block reaches the model as ordinary prose. Codex noted on SB-ASK-003 that this removes a structural cue that attacker-controlled text was quoted rather than asserted. The system prompt still declares all evidence untrusted, so no trust boundary changes. Keeping the markers would be a design change beyond this defect.
Setext underlines (=== under a heading line) are consumed by the rule pattern, flattening setext headings. Pre-existing scope, now operative.

Carried forward, not addressed: the coverage-boundary assertion all(r['term_coverage'] >= 0.30 for r in got) is vacuous on the zero-row iteration; and phrase_bonus, all_terms_bonus, the 0.30 floor, bm25 weights, the execute_match candidate limit and the fts_token prefix threshold remain unpinned.

Tilde (~~~) fences and lines of four or more backticks are still not recognised as fences, so a comment or rule inside them IS stripped. That removes the marker and its own text only; since repair 1 it can no longer consume the rest of the note. Pre-existing scope.
A 4-space indented code block is not recognised as code, so a comment or rule inside it is stripped on the same terms. Pre-existing scope, now operative, and non-destructive since repair 1.
After a comment closes mid-line, what remains on that line is treated as text rather than re-tested as a fence delimiter. Either reading is defensible; this one is declared rather than pinned.

superseded_candidates.reason: the fence test ran before the open-comment check, so a fence delimiter inside a comment toggled the fence and the comment's closing marker was never found. A terminated comment containing a fence leaked its text into the evidence; a terminated comment whose --> fell on a fence-looking line deleted the rest of the note. Four further shapes where an unterminated marker deleted the rest of a note were undeclared.

the give-back buffer introduced in repair 1 restored the raw line, so a complete comment sharing a line with a surviving opener was resurrected into the indexed body - D1 re-opened by the fix for the destruction. Separately, an opener on a rule line was destroyed rather than given back.

repair_1.trigger: Agent C FAIL on 44e75883, findings B1a (leak) and B1b (destruction), both verified independently before changing anything
repair_1.agent_c_diagnosis_accepted: the line-local claim about the PATTERNS was true and I leaned on it as if it proved the STATE MACHINE correct. It does not. Attempts 1-3 destroyed text with a regex; attempt 4 destroyed it with a state variable.
changes: an open comment is resolved BEFORE the fence test: a fence delimiter inside a comment is comment text, not a delimiter

a comment may only remove text it actually encloses. Every line an open comment claims is recorded, and if the closing marker never arrives all of them are given back with the text they had. This closes the class rather than the four shapes Agent C found: an unterminated marker now removes nothing, in prose, in inline code, in a tilde or four-backtick fence, and in an indented code block, and is kept as the literal text it is.

receipt_corrections_from_agent_c.limitation_5_renderer_justification: WITHDRAWN as false. The previous receipt said an unterminated comment consuming the rest of the note 'matches how a Markdown renderer treats it'. Agent C is right that CommonMark opens an HTML block only when the line BEGINS with '<!--'; a mid-line '<!--' without a closer is literal text and following paragraphs render normally. The justification was wrong, and the behaviour it excused is now fixed rather than excused.
receipt_corrections_from_agent_c.rule_threshold_sweep_item: CORRECTED. The previous sweep claimed 'rule threshold widened' was caught; only NARROWING to {4,} was caught, while {2,} and {1,} survived. A two-dash fixture line now pins widening in both directions.
receipt_corrections_from_agent_c.dropped_lines_never_buffered: CORRECTED. That property is real but is not what protects the span; the load-bearing protection is the 'if line.strip()' guard, which is pinned.

escalation.reason: Repair budget exhausted (2 of 2) with one confirmed residual open. Branch frozen and preserved; one terminal escalation, not a third repair.
escalation.agent_c_headline: The hole has NOT moved a sixth time. C1, C2 and C3 are closed on Agent C's own constructions, and 18,551 randomised adversarial notes produced zero leaks and zero destructions. The classifier and the give-back are sound.

blocking.summary: D1's contamination path is still open through note_title, which scans the raw lines before classify_markup runs and has no comment or fence state. The first '# ' line in a note becomes the title even when it sits inside a complete HTML comment.

what_is_genuinely_finished: the line-local classifier: no markup pattern can span lines
fence-aware chunking: a heading-like line inside a fence no longer splits a chunk, and the SB-ASK-003 stranding failure is closed
the give-back: an unterminated comment removes nothing, anywhere, and restores exactly the right text - verified by Agent C over 18,551 randomised notes
the D1/D4 coupling: a span cannot end on a line absent from the body
183 checks, and a 21-mutation sweep with zero survivors

recommended_next.description: Accept the candidate with T1 declared. The qualification is already written into purpose and defects_repaired above, and T1 is now a known limitation. The candidate strictly improves on the base and closes the body and heading paths. The title path stays open and is tracked.
